/********************************************************************
 *  Fused RoPE + RMSNorm – host‑only C++17 simulation
 *
 *  Author:  OpenAI ChatGPT
 *  Date:    2026‑11‑10
 *
 *  Compiles with:  g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -march=native fused_rope_rmsnorm.cpp
 *
 *  The implementation follows the CUDA execution model (blockDim=128,
 *  shared memory ≤48 KB) but runs on the CPU for easy verification.
 ********************************************************************/

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <random>
#include <algorithm>
#include <iomanip>
#include <cassert>

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- *
 *  Simple float4 type and helpers (mimic CUDA float4)            *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------- */
struct float4 {
    float x, y, z, w;
};

inline float4 load_float4(const float* src) {
    return {src[0], src[1], src[2], src[3]};
}

inline void store_float4(float* dst, const float4& v) {
    dst[0] = v.x; dst[1] = v.y; dst[2] = v.z; dst[3] = v.w;
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- *
 *  Emulated CUDA thread/block identifiers                         *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------- */
struct Dim3 {
    uint32_t x, y, z;
    constexpr Dim3(uint32_t a = 1, uint32_t b = 1, uint32_t c = 1) : x(a), y(b), z(c) {}
};

static Dim3 blockDim(128, 1, 1);   // fixed by the problem statement
static Dim3 gridDim;               // will be set in main()
static Dim3 threadIdx;
static Dim3 blockIdx;

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- *
 *  Kernel parameters                                               *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------- */
constexpr int M = 1024;   // rows
constexpr int N = 4096;   // columns (must be even for RoPE)
constexpr int K = 128;    // embedding dimension (unused directly)
constexpr int WARP_SIZE = 32;
constexpr size_t SHARED_MEM_BYTES = 48 * 1024; // 48 KiB

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- *
 *  Helper: compute cosine / sine tables for RoPE                  *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------- */
void build_rope_tables(std::vector<float>& cos_tab, std::vector<float>& sin_tab) {
    // For position i and dimension pair (2j,2j+1) we use theta = i / (10000^{2j/N})
    const float base = 10000.0f;
    const int half = N / 2;
    cos_tab.resize(M * half);
    sin_tab.resize(M * half);
    for (int i = 0; i < M; ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < half; ++j) {
            float inv_freq = std::pow(base, -static_cast<float>(2 * j) / N);
            float theta = i * inv_freq;
            cos_tab[i * half + j] = std::cos(theta);
            sin_tab[i * half + j] = std::sin(theta);
        }
    }
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- *
 *  Reference (scalar) implementation for verification             *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------- */
void reference_rope_rmsnorm(const float* input,
                            const float* cos_tab,
                            const float* sin_tab,
                            const float* weight,   // RMSNorm weight (size N)
                            float* output) {
    const float epsilon = 1e-5f;
    const int half = N / 2;
    for (int row = 0; row < M; ++row) {
        // 1) RoPE
        std::vector<float> rope(N);
        for (int j = 0; j < half; ++j) {
            float x0 = input[row * N + 2 * j];
            float x1 = input[row * N + 2 * j + 1];
            float c = cos_tab[row * half + j];
            float s = sin_tab[row * half + j];
            rope[2 * j]     = x0 * c - x1 * s;
            rope[2 * j + 1] = x0 * s + x1 * c;
        }

        // 2) RMSNorm
        float sum_sq = 0.0f;
        for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) sum_sq += rope[i] * rope[i];
        float rms = std::sqrt(sum_sq / N) + epsilon;
        for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            output[row * N + i] = (rope[i] / rms) * weight[i];
        }
    }
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- *
 *  Emulated CUDA kernel (fused RoPE + RMSNorm)                     *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------- */
void fused_kernel(const float* __restrict__ input,
                  const float* __restrict__ cos_tab,
                  const float* __restrict__ sin_tab,
                  const float* __restrict__ weight,
                  float* __restrict__ output) {
    // Shared memory (48 KiB) – used here only as a staging buffer.
    alignas(16) static uint8_t shared_mem[SHARED_MEM_BYTES];
    // We interpret it as float* for convenience.
    float* sh = reinterpret_cast<float*>(shared_mem);

    const int half = N / 2;
    const int vec4_per_row = N / 4;          // number of full float4 per row
    const int tail = N % 4;                  // 0..3 remaining scalars

    // Loop over blocks (gridDim.x is set in main)
    for (blockIdx.x = 0; blockIdx.x < gridDim.x; ++blockIdx.x) {
        // Each block processes a contiguous chunk of rows.
        // Rows per block = ceil(M / gridDim.x)
        const int rows_per_block = (M + gridDim.x - 1) / gridDim.x;
        const int row_start = blockIdx.x * rows_per_block;
        const int row_end   = std::min(row_start + rows_per_block, M);

        // Each thread works on a subset of columns inside a row.
        // We use a simple strided schedule: thread t handles columns
        //   col = t, t+blockDim.x, t+2*blockDim.x, ...
        for (int row = row_start; row < row_end; ++row) {
            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // 1) Load a tile of the row into shared memory (vectorised)
            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // Each thread loads up to one float4 per iteration.
            for (int vec = threadIdx.x; vec < vec4_per_row; vec += blockDim.x) {
                const float* src = input + row * N + vec * 4;
                float4 v = load_float4(src);
                // store to shared memory (still vectorised)
                float* dst = sh + vec * 4;
                store_float4(dst, v);
            }
            // Tail elements (if any) are loaded scalar‑wise by the first few threads.
            if (tail && threadIdx.x < tail) {
                int col = vec4_per_row * 4 + threadIdx.x;
                sh[col] = input[row * N + col];
            }

            // Ensure all loads complete before we start using shared memory.
            // (In real CUDA we would __syncthreads(); here a barrier is not needed
            // because we are single‑threaded per block in the host simulation.)

            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // 2) Apply RoPE + RMSNorm on‑the‑fly and write result
            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // Compute RMS of the whole row (need a reduction).  We'll let
            // thread 0 do the reduction for simplicity.
            float row_rms = 0.0f;
            if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
                float sum_sq = 0.0f;
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
                    float v = sh[i];
                    sum_sq += v * v;
                }
                row_rms = std::sqrt(sum_sq / N) + 1e-5f; // epsilon
                // broadcast to other threads via shared memory
                sh[0] = row_rms; // reuse first element as broadcast slot
            }
            // Simple spin‑wait for broadcast (host simulation, instantly visible)
            // In real CUDA we would __syncthreads(); here we just read.
            row_rms = sh[0];

            // Now each thread writes its portion of the output.
            for (int vec = threadIdx.x; vec < vec4_per_row; vec += blockDim.x) {
                // Load the original values (still in shared memory)
                const float* src = sh + vec * 4;
                float4 v = load_float4(src);

                // Apply RoPE pair‑wise inside this float4.
                // Since N is a multiple of 4, the pair boundaries align.
                // We'll treat the 4 values as two (x0,x1) and (x2,x3) pairs.
                int pair_base = vec * 4; // column index of first element in this float4
                for (int p = 0; p < 2; ++p) {
                    int idx0 = pair_base + 2 * p;
                    int idx1 = idx0 + 1;
                    // locate the corresponding cosine/sine (half dimension index)
                    int half_idx = idx0 / 2; // integer division
                    float c = cos_tab[row * half + half_idx];
                    float s = sin_tab[row * half + half_idx];
                    float x0 = (p == 0) ? v.x : v.z;
                    float x1 = (p == 0) ? v.y : v.w;
                    float y0 = x0 * c - x1 * s;
                    float y1 = x0 * s + x1 * c;
                    if (p == 0) { v.x = y0; v.y = y1; }
                    else        { v.z = y0; v.w = y1; }
                }

                // RMSNorm and weight
                v.x = (v.x / row_rms) * weight[pair_base];
                v.y = (v.y / row_rms) * weight[pair_base + 1];
                v.z = (v.z / row_rms) * weight[pair_base + 2];
                v.w = (v.w / row_rms) * weight[pair_base + 3];

                // Store to global output
                float* dst = output + row * N + vec * 4;
                store_float4(dst, v);
            }

            // Tail scalar handling (if N not multiple of 4)
            if (tail) {
                for (int col = vec4_per_row * 4 + threadIdx.x; col < N; col += blockDim.x) {
                    float x = sh[col];
                    int half_idx = col / 2;
                    float c = cos_tab[row * half + half_idx];
                    float s = sin_tab[row * half + half_idx];
                    // Determine partner index (col ^ 1 flips the LSB)
                    int partner = col ^ 1;
                    float x_partner = sh[partner];
                    // Apply rotation (the formula works for both even/odd col)
                    float y = (col % 2 == 0) ? (x * c - x_partner * s)
                                            : (x_partner * c + x * s);
                    // RMSNorm & weight
                    y = (y / row_rms) * weight[col];
                    output[row * N + col] = y;
                }
            }

            // No need for __syncthreads() at end of row because each row is independent.
        }
    }
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- *
 *  Main – generate data, run kernel, verify                         *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------- */
int main() {
    // Seed RNG
    std::mt19937 rng(42);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dist(-1.0f, 1.0f);

    // Allocate buffers
    std::vector<float> input(M * N);
    std::vector<float> weight(N);
    std::vector<float> output_fused(M * N, 0.0f);
    std::vector<float> output_ref(M * N, 0.0f);
    std::vector<float> cos_tab, sin_tab;

    for (auto& v : input)  v = dist(rng);
    for (auto& v : weight) v = dist(rng);

    // Build RoPE tables
    build_rope_tables(cos_tab, sin_tab);
    assert(cos_tab.size() == M * (N / 2));
    assert(sin_tab.size() == M * (N / 2));

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    // Determine grid size (must respect shared‑memory budget)
    // Each block uses at most 48 KiB, we already stay within that.
    // We'll launch enough blocks so each has at most 8 rows (arbitrary).
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    const int rows_per_block = 8;
    gridDim.x = (M + rows_per_block - 1) / rows_per_block;

    // Run fused kernel (host simulation)
    fused_kernel(input.data(),
                 cos_tab.data(),
                 sin_tab.data(),
                 weight.data(),
                 output_fused.data());

    // Run reference implementation
    reference_rope_rmsnorm(input.data(),
                           cos_tab.data(),
                           sin_tab.data(),
                           weight.data(),
                           output_ref.data());

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    // Verification
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    const float atol = 1e-5f;
    const float rtol = 1e-4f;
    bool ok = true;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < output_fused.size(); ++i) {
        float a = output_fused[i];
        float b = output_ref[i];
        float diff = std::fabs(a - b);
        float tol = atol + rtol * std::fabs(b);
        if (diff > tol) {
            std::cerr << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6)
                      << "Mismatch at idx " << i
                      << ": fused=" << a << " ref=" << b
                      << " diff=" << diff << " tol=" << tol << "\n";
            ok = false;
            break;
        }
    }

    std::cout << (ok ? "PASS\n" : "FAIL\n");
    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}
```

**Complexity Note**

*Time* – The kernel touches each element a constant number of times (one load, one RoPE rotation, one RMSNorm scaling, one store). Hence the overall computational complexity is **O(M · N)**.

*Space* – Global buffers store `2·M·N + N + 2·M·(N/2)` floats ≈ 2 × 4 MiB for the given dimensions. Shared memory usage is bounded by the 48 KB budget (the static `shared_mem` array). No additional dynamic allocations are performed per‑thread.

        if (p.z > 0) { face = 2; u = -p.x / p.z; v = -p.y / p.z; }
        else        { face = 5; u =  p.x / p.z; v =  p.y / p.z; }
    }
    // Clamp to [-1,1] (numerical safety)
    u = std::max(-1.0, std::min(1.0, u));
    v = std::max(-1.0, std::min(1.0, v));
    return {face, u, v};
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// (u,v) ∈ [-1,1] → (s,t) ∈ [0,1] → integer (i,j) at given level
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
inline uint32_t StToIJ(double s) {
    // s in [0,1], map to integer in [0, 2^kMaxLevel-1]
    uint64_t n = static_cast<uint64_t>(std::floor(s * (1ULL << kMaxLevel)));
    if (n >= (1ULL << kMaxLevel)) n = (1ULL << kMaxLevel) - 1;
    return static_cast<uint32_t>(n);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Hilbert curve utilities (xy <-> d)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
uint64_t xy2d(uint32_t x, uint32_t y) {
    uint64_t d = 0;
    for (int s = kMaxLevel - 1; s >= 0; --s) {
        uint64_t rx = (x >> s) & 1ULL;
        uint64_t ry = (y >> s) & 1ULL;
        d += ((3ULL * rx) ^ ry) << (2 * s);
        // rotate
        if (ry == 0) {
            if (rx == 1) {
                x = (1U << kMaxLevel) - 1 - x;
                y = (1U << kMaxLevel) - 1 - y;
            }
            std::swap(x, y);
        }
    }
    return d;
}

void d2xy(uint64_t d, uint32_t& x, uint32_t& y) {
    x = y = 0;
    for (int s = 0; s < kMaxLevel; ++s) {
        uint64_t rx = (d >> (2 * s + 1)) & 1ULL;
        uint64_t ry = (d >> (2 * s)) & 1ULL;
        // rotate
        if (ry == 0) {
            if (rx == 1) {
                x = (1U << s) - 1 - x;
                y = (1U << s) - 1 - y;
            }
            std::swap(x, y);
        }
        x += static_cast<uint32_t>(rx) << s;
        y += static_cast<uint32_t>(ry) << s;
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Encode a cell (face, i, j) into a 64‑bit S2 CellId
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
int64_t EncodeCellId(int face, uint32_t i, uint32_t j) {
    uint64_t pos = xy2d(i, j);                     // 0 … (1<<2k)-1
    // cell id layout: [face:3][pos:2k][lsb:1]  (lsb is always 1 for leaf cells)
    int64_t id = (static_cast<int64_t>(face) << (kPosBits + 1)) |
                 (static_cast<int64_t>(pos) << 1) | 1LL;
    return id;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Decode a CellId back to (face,i,j)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
void DecodeCellId(int64_t cellId, int& face, uint32_t& i, uint32_t& j) {
    assert(cellId & 1LL);               // leaf cells have lowest bit = 1
    face = static_cast<int>((cellId >> (kPosBits + 1)) & 0x7);
    uint64_t pos = static_cast<uint64_t>(cellId >> 1) & ((1ULL << kPosBits) - 1);
    d2xy(pos, i, j);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// (face,i,j) → lat/lng (center of the cell)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
std::pair<double,double> CellIdToLatLng(int64_t cellId) {
    int face; uint32_t i, j;
    DecodeCellId(cellId, face, i, j);
    // Convert i,j to (s,t) at cell centre
    double s = (static_cast<double>(i) + 0.5) / (1ULL << kMaxLevel);
    double t = (static_cast<double>(j) + 0.5) / (1ULL << kMaxLevel);
    // (s,t) → (u,v) ∈ [-1,1]
    double u = 2.0 * s - 1.0;
    double v = 2.0 * t - 1.0;

    // Inverse face‑UV → XYZ
    Vec3 p;
    switch (face) {
        case 0: p = Vec3( 1,  u,  v); break;
        case 1: p = Vec3(-u,  1,  v); break;
        case 2: p = Vec3(-u, -v,  1); break;
        case 3: p = Vec3(-1, -u, -v); break;
        case 4: p = Vec3( v, -1, -u); break;
        case 5: p = Vec3( v,  u, -1); break;
        default: p = Vec3(0,0,0); // never
    }
    p = p.normalized();

    double lat = std::asin(p.z) * kRadToDeg;
    double lng = std::atan2(p.y, p.x) * kRadToDeg;
    return {lat, lng};
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Round‑trip test for a high‑latitude point
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
int main() {
    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(12);

    // Test point: 78.22° N, 0° E (Svalbard high‑latitude zone)
    const double latDeg = 78.22;
    const double lngDeg = 0.0;

    // 1️⃣ Convert to XYZ
    Vec3 xyz = LatLngToXYZ(latDeg, lngDeg);

    // 2️⃣ Face‑UV projection
    FaceUV fu = XYZToFaceUV(xyz);
    std::cout << "Face: " << fu.face << "  u: " << fu.u << "  v: " << fu.v << "\n";

    // 3️⃣ (u,v) → (s,t) → (i,j)
    double s = (fu.u + 1.0) * 0.5;
    double t = (fu.v + 1.0) * 0.5;
    uint32_t i = StToIJ(s);
    uint32_t j = StToIJ(t);

    // 4️⃣ Encode CellId
    int64_t cellId = EncodeCellId(fu.face, i, j);
    std::cout << "CellId (hex): 0x" << std::hex << cellId << std::dec << "\n";

    // 5️⃣ Decode back to lat/lng
    auto [latBack, lngBack] = CellIdToLatLng(cellId);
    std::cout << "Decoded lat: " << latBack << "  lng: " << lngBack << "\n";

    // 6️⃣ Verify error (should be < 1e‑9 rad ≈ 1 nm)
    double dLat = std::fabs(latBack - latDeg);
    double dLng = std::fabs(lngBack - lngDeg);
    std::cout << "Δlat = " << dLat << " deg, Δlng = " << dLng << " deg\n";

    const double epsDeg = 1e-9 * kRadToDeg; // ~1 nm in degrees
    assert(dLat < epsDeg && dLng < epsDeg);
    std::cout << "Round‑trip verification passed.\n";

    return 0;
}
```

**Complexity Note**

*Encoding* and *decoding* each run in `O(kMaxLevel)` time (30 iterations) and use
`O(1)` additional memory.  All other operations are constant‑time.  The module
therefore scales linearly with the chosen S2 level and easily meets real‑time
requirements for drone photogrammetry pipelines.

// Self‑contained C++17 program computing GSD and ray‑DEM intersection.
// Compile with: g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic DronePhotogrammetry.cpp -o DronePhotogrammetry

#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <cassert>

constexpr double PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
constexpr double DEG2RAD = PI / 180.0;
constexpr double RAD2DEG = 180.0 / PI;

// WGS‑84 ellipsoid (sphere approximation for the test)
constexpr double EARTH_RADIUS = 6378137.0; // metres

// ---------- Utility Functions ----------
inline double deg2rad(double deg) { return deg * DEG2RAD; }
inline double rad2deg(double rad) { return rad * RAD2DEG; }

// Convert geodetic (lat,lon,alt) to ECEF (X,Y,Z)
// Uses the exact ellipsoidal formulas (WGS‑84)
void geodeticToECEF(double latDeg, double lonDeg, double h,
                    double& X, double& Y, double& Z)
{
    // WGS‑84 constants
    constexpr double a = 6378137.0;          // semi‑major axis
    constexpr double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563; // flattening
    constexpr double e2 = f * (2 - f);        // first eccentricity squared

    double lat = deg2rad(latDeg);
    double lon = deg2rad(lonDeg);
    double sinLat = std::sin(lat);
    double cosLat = std::cos(lat);
    double sinLon = std::sin(lon);
    double cosLon = std::cos(lon);

    double N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * sinLat * sinLat); // prime vertical radius

    X = (N + h) * cosLat * cosLon;
    Y = (N + h) * cosLat * sinLon;
    Z = (N * (1 - e2) + h) * sinLat;
}

// Compute ENU basis vectors at a given geodetic location.
// Returns unit vectors e (east), n (north), u (up) expressed in ECEF.
void enuBasis(double latDeg, double lonDeg,
              double e[3], double n[3], double u[3])
{
    double lat = deg2rad(latDeg);
    double lon = deg2rad(lonDeg);
    double sinLat = std::sin(lat);
    double cosLat = std::cos(lat);
    double sinLon = std::sin(lon);
    double cosLon = std::cos(lon);

    // East
    e[0] = -sinLon;
    e[1] =  cosLon;
    e[2] =  0.0;

    // North
    n[0] = -sinLat * cosLon;
    n[1] = -sinLat * sinLon;
    n[2] =  cosLat;

    // Up
    u[0] =  cosLat * cosLon;
    u[1] =  cosLat * sinLon;
    u[2] =  sinLat;
}

// Rotate a vector by yaw (Z), pitch (Y), roll (X) – intrinsic Tait‑Bryan angles (degrees)
// Returns the rotated vector in the same coordinate system.
void rotateVector(double v[3],
                  double yawDeg, double pitchDeg, double rollDeg,
                  double out[3])
{
    double yaw   = deg2rad(yawDeg);
    double pitch = deg2rad(pitchDeg);
    double roll  = deg2rad(rollDeg);

    double cy = std::cos(yaw),   sy = std::sin(yaw);
    double cp = std::cos(pitch), sp = std::sin(pitch);
    double cr = std::cos(roll),  sr = std::sin(roll);

    // Rotation matrix R = Rz(yaw) * Ry(pitch) * Rx(roll)
    double R[3][3] = {
        { cy*cp, cy*sp*sr - sy*cr, cy*sp*cr + sy*sr },
        { sy*cp, sy*sp*sr + cy*cr, sy*sp*cr - cy*sr },
        { -sp,   cp*sr,            cp*cr            }
    };

    out[0] = R[0][0]*v[0] + R[0][1]*v[1] + R[0][2]*v[2];
    out[1] = R[1][0]*v[0] + R[1][1]*v[1] + R[1][2]*v[2];
    out[2] = R[2][0]*v[0] + R[2][1]*v[1] + R[2][2]*v[2];
}

// ---------- Core Algorithms ----------

// 1. Ground Sample Distance (GSD)
double computeGSD(double sensorWidth,   // metres
                  int    imageWidth,    // pixels
                  double focalLength,   // metres
                  double altitude)     // metres above ellipsoid
{
    double pixelSize = sensorWidth / static_cast<double>(imageWidth); // m/pixel
    // Simple pin‑hole model (orthogonal projection)
    return (pixelSize * altitude) / focalLength;
}

// 2. Ray – Sphere (Earth) Intersection
//   origin: ECEF ray origin
//   dir   : normalized ECEF direction (must be unit length)
//   Returns true if intersection found and writes intersection point to 'Xint,Yint,Zint'.
//   The intersection closest to the origin (positive t) is returned.
bool intersectRaySphere(const double origin[3],
                        const double dir[3],
                        double radius,
                        double& Xint, double& Yint, double& Zint)
{
    // Quadratic: (o + t d)·(o + t d) = r²
    double a = dir[0]*dir[0] + dir[1]*dir[1] + dir[2]*dir[2]; // =1 if dir normalized
    double b = 2.0 * (origin[0]*dir[0] + origin[1]*dir[1] + origin[2]*dir[2]);
    double c = origin[0]*origin[0] + origin[1]*origin[1] + origin[2]*origin[2] - radius*radius;

    // Discriminant
    double disc = b*b - 4*a*c;
    if (disc < 0.0) return false; // no intersection

    // Numerically stable quadratic solution
    double sqrtDisc = std::sqrt(disc);
    double q = (b > 0) ? -0.5 * (b + sqrtDisc) : -0.5 * (b - sqrtDisc);
    double t0 = q / a;
    double t1 = c / q;

    double t = (t0 > 0) ? t0 : t1; // choose the positive smallest t
    if (t < 0) return false;      // both intersections behind the origin

    Xint = origin[0] + t * dir[0];
    Yint = origin[1] + t * dir[1];
    Zint = origin[2] + t * dir[2];
    return true;
}

// Convert ECEF back to geodetic (lat,lon,alt) – iterative Bowring method.
void ecefToGeodetic(double X, double Y, double Z,
                    double& latDeg, double& lonDeg, double& h)
{
    constexpr double a = 6378137.0;
    constexpr double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563;
    constexpr double e2 = f * (2 - f);
    constexpr double ep2 = e2 / (1 - e2);

    double lon = std::atan2(Y, X);
    double p = std::hypot(X, Y);
    double theta = std::atan2(Z * a, p * (1 - f) * a);
    double sinTheta = std::sin(theta);
    double cosTheta = std::cos(theta);

    double lat = std::atan2(Z + ep2 * (1 - f) * a * sinTheta * sinTheta * sinTheta,
                           p - e2 * a * cosTheta * cosTheta * cosTheta);
    double N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * std::sin(lat) * std::sin(lat));
    double alt = p / std::cos(lat) - N;

    // One more iteration for higher accuracy (optional)
    double latPrev = 0.0;
    while (std::abs(lat - latPrev) > 1e-12) {
        latPrev = lat;
        N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * std::sin(lat) * std::sin(lat));
        alt = p / std::cos(lat) - N;
        lat = std::atan2(Z, p * (1 - e2 * N / (N + alt)));
    }

    latDeg = rad2deg(lat);
    lonDeg = rad2deg(lon);
    h = alt;
}
